reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that dribble success hinges on two critical biomechanical factors: the attacker's balance (B_a) and the angular alignment (A_{ad}) between attacker and defender. These are extracted from 3D pose tracking data, which captures body posture and orientation in real time. The balance score B_a is computed from joint angles and center-of-mass displacement, while A_{ad} reflects the directional mismatch between attacker and defender. These features are then embedded into a logistic regression model that combines them with traditional 2D positional data. The resulting model shows improved predictive power because it accounts for non-linearities in movement dynamics that 2D data misses. The failure mode occurs when either B_a falls below a threshold (indicating instability) or A_{ad} exceeds π/2 radians (indicating misalignment), both of which correlate with unsuccessful dribbles. This dual-factor model represents a shift from static position-based metrics to dynamic biomechanical ones, aligning with recent advances in sports analytics.
